title: Sabbath Afternoon Class: Betrayers & Secret Admirers

sense.text:
“For God created man to be immortal, and made him to be an image of his own eternity.” The whole purpose when God created us was for us to live forever, and we are made expressly after his image.

So if we are all made after the image of God, what is it to envy against each other? Each and every one of us has that dispensation, that spirit put upon us. We are made after the image of the greatest entity, the creator of all things, so how can you envy each other?

“Nevertheless through envy of the devil came death into the world: and they that do hold of his side do find it.” They that hold of the side of the devil, with that spirit of envy, are going to find death. Something had to happen for a man made after God’s image to let envy step in, and that is where this class goes.

“Now the serpent was more subtil than any beast of the field.” This is an allegory, and nothing here is at face value; there is a mystery behind it. To be subtil is to be cunning. If you want to deceive somebody, you find the thing that will trigger that person to respond a certain way: you phrase a comment or ask a question that is bait, to lure them in.

“Yea, hath God said, Ye shall not eat of every tree of the garden?” He already knew the answer. That was the subtilty: you bring it in with a bait question, the same thing Satan did with Christ. Sometimes a question is just bait, to see if you will nibble on it. When somebody passes ten other people to come and ask you a question that seems off, ask why.

She answered him, and her answer was right: God said do not eat of it, neither touch it, lest ye die. But the smart thing was not to answer at all. She already knew the answer, and she took the bait. This touches dealing with the other nations, which is another class.

“Ye shall not surely die.” Here comes the subtilty: first the bait in a question, then, you ain’t gonna die. Eve had an itching ear. He knew something about her that let him say certain trigger things to get her to betray God.

“Ye shall be as gods, knowing good and evil.” That was her trigger: she wanted to be equal, to be a god. He saw that she was not content, and he triggered her there. Brothers and sisters have trigger points too. You want a wife or a husband, and Satan sends the person that seems ideally like what you like, to bait you. It is small pieces to a big puzzle that bait you into a certain thing, and people are blinded to it.

“The tree was good for food.” That is what sin is: sin feels good, that is why you do it. Whatever the sin, lust or hatred, it activates something inside you that you perceive as good, and you betray God to fulfil it. There is a price to pay.

“She took of the fruit thereof, and did eat, and gave also unto her husband with her; and he did eat.” On earth there is nothing stronger than what is between a woman’s legs. Men will kill each other over that, rob, steal, sell crack, and sin against the God that made them. Zerubbabel said it: the only thing to defeat that is wisdom, God’s words. You need something spiritual to defeat that earthly demon. A man will take his last dollar to a strip club to pay a woman to take off her clothes when he has a wife at home. That is insanity, that is madness.

Of all the works of the flesh, one in particular: “emulations”. Many times betrayers betray because they have a spirit of emulation. It is a sad existence to live your life looking at another person’s life and desiring to be them, secretly hating them because you want what they have. It is one thing to covet the best gifts, to be a better teacher. But to secretly hate a sister because she has nice hair or a nice ring: that spirit of emulation has destroyed many people. It is a cunning demon. You are a secret admirer of somebody, and you plot and you scheme.

“They which do such things shall not inherit the kingdom of God.” That was Eve. Eve wanted to be like Adam; she wanted to be a god, to emulate the man and have dominion. That is not how God set women up to be, and because of that spirit of emulation death was issued into the earth.

God said, I made you after my image: you hit lotto. But in that image he has different people for different reasons, and some are not happy with the course they are called into. Then they plot and scheme, trying to be something God did not make them to be, at least not at that point of their life.
Korah is the son of Izhar, the son of Kohath, the son of Levi: near kin to Moses. His own near kin rose up against him.

“Two hundred and fifty princes of the assembly, famous in the congregation, men of renown.” These were not regular men; they had a name. All of this to go up against Moses, right after the Lord brought them out of Egypt and through the sea. How were they able to gather 250 renowned men against Moses, and why?

“Mark them which cause divisions and offences.” Those are the “such” of verse 18. These are key indicating signs for us today. When you are in this body and you see somebody trying to cause division, whispering, murmuring, gossiping, pulling people to their side, you should know what is coming out of that mouth.

If what you are doing is of God, you don’t have to hide it; you can say it openly, because you are speaking the oracles of God. But I’ll call you later, I’ll text you later? If you fall for that, you are simple. Even renowned brothers who have been around a while get caught, because the one baiting them can see something in them. A brother once asked another brother at the Sabbath to go to a strip club after: he had to have seen something in him to say that. That is contingency talk, clique talk, birds of a feather, and that clique stuff supersedes the love of God.

If your conversation is not one of bringing solutions, even when there is a real problem in the body, you are part of the problem. God will sort it out; that is his job. Your job is to gather the 12 tribes. God will remove who he wants to remove.

“And avoid them.” Which part of that don’t we understand?

“For they that are such serve not our Lord Jesus Christ, but their own belly; and by good words and fair speeches deceive the hearts of the simple.” The 250 renowned men were simple men. They had made bricks in Egypt, seen the sea opened and closed on their enemies, and then followed a man who could only talk. Show me you open the ocean. Christ came back from the dead; beat that one. You know them by their fruits: these talkers have little or no fruit in this body, and the simple fall for it.

“And they gathered themselves together against Moses and against Aaron”: the 250 renowned men with Korah and Dathan. “Ye take too much upon you, seeing all the congregation are holy.” They felt confident because they said something true. People will use the Bible to deceive you. But if you keep the commandments and study, you have a discerning spirit: yes, the Bible says that, but not in that context. Study to show thyself approved, rightly dividing the word. If an understanding nullifies all the other precepts, it is not right, because the Bible does not contradict itself.

precepts.why:
This is where they got it from. When Israel came out of Egypt, God told them, “ye shall be unto me a kingdom of priests, and an holy nation.” That is why they felt they could say “all the congregation are holy”.

But there is still a hierarchy in it. They told Moses, we priests too, you ain’t the only one, and all 250 said, word, God did say that. Meanwhile the ringleaders, Dathan and Korah, got them. There are many men and women today who would do the same thing: betrayers.

sense.text: When Moses heard their charge he fell upon his face (Numbers 16:4): that’s what you think of me? They painted Moses as acting better than everybody else, a smear campaign to destroy his name, though Moses never said that. This is what those men struggled with: “all members have not the same office.” They don’t understand that.

“Whether prophecy, let us prophesy according to the proportion of faith”: whatever God has inspired you with, run with that. You are made after his image, so it is all good, but he is not going to give any of us all of it, or you would be God. He makes us all work together, each with a piece. Those men tried to outshine Moses, and that is not what they were called for.

“Or ministry, let us wait on our ministering.” Some people cannot wait on their ministry; they are speeding. God sets people in this body where he wants them. Either you roll with it, glorify God and be grateful, or you buck against it and find yourself out in the wilderness doing your own thing. Choose the first one.
“Ye take too much upon you, ye sons of Levi.” Korah is the son of Kohath, from the family of the high priest, and Moses is his near kin, and still he could not wait on his ministry.

“Seemeth it but a small thing unto you, that the God of Israel hath separated you from the congregation of Israel”? To be the priest, the mouthpiece to God, was not enough for them; they wanted more. All of us are created after the image of God. Whatever part you have in that, be content. Those who are not become betrayers, and they will try to tear apart everything because they are not what they think they are.
“And seek ye the priesthood also?”

“For which cause both thou and all thy company are gathered together against the Lord.” Moses is telling them, you ain’t really coming against me, you are coming against God; the Lord set this up. And “what is Aaron”? Aaron is near kin to you too, and he is the one God chose. They came in with the machine already moving. God chose Moses to go before Pharaoh and chose Aaron, whose rod budded, not Korah or Dathan. They were fighting against God. Those men were betrayers, evil as hell.

“Is it a small thing that thou hast brought us up out of a land that floweth with milk and honey, to kill us in the wilderness”? God was bringing down quail, giving them water out of a rock, feeding them with manna, and they had seen the sea open. They were complaining, looking for problems, and because it was not moving the way they wanted it to move, they conspired.

“And they took every man his censer, and put fire in them, and laid incense thereon.” Two hundred and fifty men lit their censers to burn incense to God, sure that God was with them and that they would show Moses. In their minds God was going to smell it and show them favour.

precepts.why:
“I hate, I despise your feast days, and I will not smell in your solemn assemblies.” God said, I ain’t smelling nothing, I’m about to kill you. They thought they had a plug with God. Moses had the direct connect: I have not dealt with them unjustly. And God said, let them burn it; I am not smelling that, you are not pleasing me.

So you have betrayers who betray the men set up over them and then think they have a connect with God. It don’t work like that. You sneaky, slimy little bastard.

sense.text: “Depart, I pray you, from the tents of these wicked men, and touch nothing of theirs.” There is the warning: get away from these men. It is the same as Romans 16: mark them which cause division, and avoid them.

“Dathan and Abiram came out, and stood in the door of their tents, and their wives, and their sons, and their little children.” Their wives should have bounced: you’re on your own on this one, kids let’s go. But they stood there in their folly. Many women follow their husbands into the abyss and take their kids along for the ride.
“But if the Lord make a new thing, and the earth open her mouth”: God made a new thing on earth and opened a pit for them. They forgot they were dealing with God’s anointed.

“And there came out a fire from the Lord, and consumed the two hundred and fifty men that offered incense.” For the 250 God chose a different death: fire. The end result of this history: do not be a betrayer, and don’t follow wicked men into foolishness to bring division.

precepts.why: “Enviest thou for my sake? would God that all the Lord’s people were prophets.” Moses was not acting like he was the only one. Men were trying to stop others from prophesying, and Moses said, don’t envy for my sake; I wish they all were prophets. He was not keeping it to himself; it was just what God chose. Korah’s men conspired an evil conspiracy anyway, betrayers, and found themselves dead.

sense.text: This is an allegory. “O that thou wert as my brother, that sucked the breasts of my mother!” That is how close we were: we both fed off our mother’s breast. “When I should find thee without, I would kiss thee”: when you lacked, I was always there for you. “Yea, I should not be despised”: there is no reason for you to despise me, because we are supposed to be this close.

“Set me as a seal upon thine heart, as a seal upon thine arm”: that is wisdom; that is what the whole book is about.

“Jealousy is cruel as the grave.” As close as we are supposed to be, here rises the spirit of jealousy. The grave is cruel because it holds you; it doesn’t let you go. That is how jealousy is: it holds some people so bad they can’t fight it. It has captured them. To all who walk around with that spirit of jealousy secretly inside them, with hatred: that is a loser’s life. Especially a man: that is weak, super effeminate, to go to sleep and wake up thinking about another man.

“The coals thereof are coals of fire, which hath a most vehement flame.” Coal burns long and hot and keeps going. That is jealousy: it slowly sucks all the righteousness out of your spirit. You were made after his image, but envy took whatever was good in you and left you lacking. That is a sad existence of a life.
“Abel was a keeper of sheep, but Cain was a tiller of the ground.” Two different offices, and neither is better than the other.

“In process of time”: that process of time was when Cain slowly built up a spirit of hatred towards his blood brother. It did not happen overnight. Sometimes a brother is in five, seven, ten years and then bugs out: all that time they were becoming hardened, jealous, envious and covetous.

“Cain brought of the fruit of the ground”: he brought fruits, but not the firstfruits. That is what he did wrong.

“Abel, he also brought of the firstlings of his flock”, and “the Lord had respect unto Abel and to his offering.” A lot of times when people suffer from jealousy, envy and betrayal, it is because there is underlying sin in them, unbeknownst to you, and it provokes and activates these other spirits. They are not living to their full potential, they know it, and they direct their anger at the person they wish they could be. But they could do it; they just have to be righteous.
“But unto Cain and to his offering he had not respect.” Cain sinned against God, and then he was mad at Abel because he himself didn’t do right.

precepts.why: “Honour the Lord with thy substance, and with the firstfruits of all thine increase.” This is what Cain did wrong: he brought fruits, but not the firstfruits of his increase, while Abel brought the firstlings of his flock.

“But the firstling of a cow, or the firstling of a sheep, or the firstling of a goat, thou shalt not redeem; they are holy.” The firstlings are holy; they go to the Lord. Cain did not honour God with the firstfruits of the ground; he brought whatever he wanted to bring.

When God blesses us with money or whatever we have, we re-up with God and he keeps giving, and the flow keeps going. You don’t draw from the well and put nothing back. God ain’t giving nothing for nothing: he gives to you so you can help build his thing.

sense.text: “And Cain was very wroth, and his countenance fell.” God gave him everything and asked only the firstfruits. Cain did not honour him and still wanted God to be pleased. He could not be wroth with God, because he could not get to him, so he directed it at the righteous man. People project their own faults and their anger on somebody else, like Korah: Moses, you think you’re better than us. Moses never said that.

“If thou doest well, shalt thou not be accepted?” Bring the firstfruits like I asked, and I accept it. “And if thou doest not well, sin lieth at the door.” That door is not your front door; it is your head. Satan is in your head governing you, only because you didn’t do what you were supposed to do. Wisdom cannot dwell in a body subject to sin. Over a process of time hatred, jealousy and envy took hold of him.

“And Cain talked with Abel his brother.” He was not talking reckless; he was talking peaceable: hey, what’s up. He was angry, but secretly. He kept the hatred in his spirit and smiled in his face, and when he had the opportunity and his brother was alone, he rose up and slew him.

A whore hates to see a godly woman: who does she think she is, she thinks she’s better. That is the same way Cain was angry with Abel. Do what you are supposed to do, and don’t be mad at the righteous because you ain’t right.

“So shall righteousness hate iniquity, when she decketh herself.” The righteous are supposed to hate iniquity the way the whore hates honest women: they can’t stand them. The same way, we are not supposed to stand iniquity.

“For the ungodly said, reasoning with themselves, but not aright.” That was the 250 princes with Moses: the ungodly get together and reason, and they think they are using the Bible, and they use it all wrong. Look at their fruits: zero. They come up shrivelled up and dead.

“Our life is short and tedious, and in the death of a man there is no remedy.” Many people live for this present time, as if this life were the end. So they say, let’s live it up right now. They are not reasoning aright.
“Let our strength be the law of justice”: we can dictate, we have the voice, we have the power. “That which is feeble is found to be nothing worth”: in their eyes, the righteous can do nothing.

“We are esteemed of him as counterfeits.” The godly esteem them as counterfeits. All Israel is not Israel: they might have fringes on, but that don’t mean they are right. The godly recognise them and are not caught by their fair speeches.

“He pronounceth the end of the just to be blessed, and maketh his boast that God is his father.” The end of the just is blessed.

“Let us see if his words be true.” Their bright idea is to try to kill him, to see if God helps him. They are still not reasoning aright, living as though life only exists in the present. After this is when it really counts, when you have to come back and answer to the Father.

“Let us condemn him with a shameful death.” They are so mad, and the man did nothing to them; he just won’t roll with them because they are counterfeit. You want to destroy another man because your life ain’t together, but it could be together.
“For their own wickedness hath blinded them.” They don’t discern “a reward for blameless souls” because Satan has them, and they are so far gone they can’t see it.

“For God created man to be immortal.” God made you in his image. If you are moving in envy, that is your choice. Evil will try to pull you into evil, and if it can’t pull you in, it will try to kill you, destroy your name, or destroy you.

“Nevertheless through envy of the devil came death into the world.” God made us immortal, the sons of God, and what do they turn into? A jealous, hateful demon, of no use to God. All they can think is, we only got one life, YOLO. Envy is so bad that brothers will make music videos outside the school with the IUIC logo behind them. That is rottenness to the bone. You shall know them by their fruits.
“Behold, what manner of love the Father hath bestowed upon us, that we should be called the sons of God.” Out of all that love, you turn around and learn to hate your brother?
“We shall be like him; for we shall see him as he is.” We are going to be like the one that created everything. There is power in that.

“And every man that hath this hope in him purifieth himself, even as he is pure.” If you have the hope that you will be like him, made in his express image, the sons of God, you purify yourself. If you don’t get the hate, envy and jealousy out of your spirit, you never really believed. You were here under pretence, lying in wait, feeding on demonic forces, until you became a full-grown demon.

“Little children, let no man deceive you: he that doeth righteousness is righteous.” Don’t get caught by the fair speeches, the look, the grey beard. You don’t have to figure it out: look in the Bible at what is righteous, then look at what he does. His actions are the fruit. Mark them that cause division, and avoid them. Two hundred and fifty princes, men of renown, got caught up and were put to death.

“For the devil sinneth from the beginning.” Through envy of the devil came death. From the beginning Satan’s game was to divide us: put Eve against Adam, and get Adam to move away from the true living God. Don’t bring a man tales about a brother; he will call that brother and let both of you answer. You can’t program a man of God except with the word.

“That he might destroy the works of the devil.” The works of the devil are to keep us in sin. Christ was manifested to give us the understanding of the laws and to gather the 12 tribes of Israel. Satan’s job is to teach you to sin and keep the 12 tribes scattered. So if you are not part of gathering the 12 tribes, you are a betrayer of your nation, a secret admirer sitting amongst us looking to destroy, and God is going to kill you.
“Whosoever doeth not righteousness is not of God, neither he that loveth not his brother.” That is it. Who would want to destroy their brother or their sister?

“Not as Cain, who was of that wicked one, and slew his brother.” He slew him “because his own works were evil, and his brother’s righteous.” He hated because he was not like him, but he could have been, because he was made after God’s express image. He chose to be evil, and then wanted to destroy that which is righteous.
“Whosoever hateth his brother is a murderer.” You hate your brother so much that you want to murder him. God made us in his image to be immortal, and “no murderer hath eternal life abiding in him.”
“The spirit that dwelleth in us lusteth to envy.” Do you think the scripture says that in vain? It is not there by accident. There is something in us, and it is there for a reason.
“But he giveth more grace.” He gives us grace to get over that spirit of envy and hatred; he gives us space to fix it. This class is for somebody battling that right now, and it is for all of us.

“Draw nigh to God, and he will draw nigh to you.” Call on God and he will give you a way to overcome the spirit of emulation, envy and jealousy, and take away the spirit of being a betrayer.

“Purify your hearts, ye double minded.” The double-minded man sits in here bouncing back and forth in his mind. They put on the garment and come every Sabbath, and secretly they have hatred. They want to be here, but they murmur and talk about you; they watch class and take notes, and they murmur. That is madness.

precepts.why: We just read it in First John: “every man that hath this hope in him purifieth himself, even as he is pure.” Drawing nigh to God is purifying yourself.

sense.text: “But if ye have bitter envying and strife in your hearts.” Not just envy: bitter envy. Bitter means resentful: feeling bitterness or indignation at having been treated unfairly. They feel they are not getting a fair shake, that they were dealt with wrong. That is the mind corrupted, building up resentment out of envy: why does he have her, she should be my wife; why does he have that job, that house; why is he the elder? A man bitter like that is effeminate.
“This wisdom descendeth not from above, but is earthly, sensual, devilish.” It will convince you, it feels good, and it will make you justify your actions. But the base behind it is envy.

“Saul hath slain his thousands, and David his ten thousands.” The Most High had just given them victory over the Philistines, enemies who would have put all of them in captivity, and the saying displeased Saul. He was the king, ruling. Why upset? Envy and jealousy.

David was Saul’s armourbearer. In war the armourbearer carries your other swords and finishes off everyone you strike and leave behind, so David had more kills just from finishing them for Saul. Saul was old and the king; he could have let the young man have his praise. Instead, here came the jealousy.
“What can he have more but the kingdom?”
“And Saul eyed David from that day and forward.” Jealousy and envy come from something already in the person: prior sin that takes away the discerning spirit. That was Cain, and that was Saul.

precepts.why: God told Saul to “utterly destroy all that they have, and spare them not”: kill everything. But Saul and the people spared Agag and the best of the sheep and oxen, keeping the king and what was good and destroying everything vile.

“For rebellion is as the sin of witchcraft, and stubbornness is as iniquity and idolatry.” God made him king and he didn’t listen; he was stubborn and rebellious. Witchcraft is about controlling a person’s mind so they do your bidding, like Genesis: his desire shall be to thee, and thou shalt rule over him. Satan entered into Saul, he listened, and he was stubborn against the God who anointed him, so God took the throne from him.

This is the thought process behind his behaviour: he sinned against God, his spirit wasn’t right, jealousy jumped on him, and he directed his anger at a godly man.
“But the Spirit of the Lord departed from Saul, and an evil spirit from the Lord troubled him.”

When the evil spirit was upon Saul, “David took an harp, and played with his hand: so Saul was refreshed.” David was amongst him and would play the harp to subdue that evil spirit, but it was deep in him.

sense.text: “The soul of Jonathan was knit with the soul of David, and Jonathan loved him as his own soul.” Imagine Saul seeing his son and David so close.

precepts.why: “So David prevailed over the Philistine with a sling and with a stone.” This is what brought them to be knit together.

“And David took the head of the Philistine, and brought it to Jerusalem.” Everybody saw it, all the women saw it. David got fame and built a relationship with Saul’s son, and slowly Satan crept in: he is more important than me, people like him more than me, my son is close with him.

They both had the same enemy, the Philistines, and Saul couldn’t see it; he was simple as hell. Today we all fight against our enemies, and then we are jealous of each other in here trying to destroy each other. Don’t we have a bigger enemy to fight?

sense.text: David played the harp as at other times, to quiet the spirit, but Saul had a javelin in his hand. David was fighting Saul’s wars, killing his enemies and protecting him, and still Saul betrayed him and turned against him.

“And Saul cast the javelin.” The harp was not subduing that spirit any more. It was growing and percolating, and he couldn’t control it. The hatred had laid dormant a long time, but his spirit was not right, and now it was manifesting in his behaviour until nothing could stop him.
“And Saul was afraid of David, because the Lord was with him.” He realised God was with this man.

“Therefore Saul removed him from him, and made him his captain over a thousand.” David had been close, playing the harp in Saul’s personal space as a bodyguard. Saul sent him out as a captain, “and he went out and came in before the people.” The Most High is the master chess player. When you think you are making a master move, God is making you do it for his bigger plan. This is spiritual.
“And David behaved himself wisely in all his ways.” David wasn’t plotting against Saul. He did the job he was sent to do.

“But all Israel and Judah loved David, because he went out and came in before them.” Sending him out built his relationship with the people and set him up to become king. With a jealous spirit you are kicking against the pricks; you will not stop the Most High’s mission.

“Let not mine hand be upon him, but let the hand of the Philistines be upon him.” Saul wanted him dead, sending him into battle to be killed by the very enemy trying to destroy the nation. That is how much hatred he had.
Merab, who was promised, “was given unto Adriel the Meholathite to wife.” Saul broke his covenant with David.
“I will give him her, that she may be a snare to him.” Saul knew his daughter. He would make David’s life miserable at home so his head would not be in the fight. That is hatred.

“Take ye heed every one of his neighbour, and trust ye not in any brother: for every brother will utterly supplant.” To supplant is to supersede and replace, to usurp, to displace. It will be the ones closest to you who try to undermine you, topple you and destroy you. Either listen to what God is saying here, or do it your way and see how it works out. It doesn’t.

“One Simon of the tribe of Benjamin, who was made governor of the temple, fell out with the high priest about disorder in the city.” When he could not overcome Onias, who had a good name, he went to the enemy and snitched, telling him about the money in the treasury, just because he couldn’t have his way. That is an effeminate man. He didn’t even go at Onias one-on-one; he did something to the detriment of the whole nation: if I can’t have it, I’ll burn it all down. We live these scriptures: men who are mad will rip the whole thing apart and not care about anybody else’s children or family.
Two young men “scourged him continually, and gave him many sore stripes”: the angels whipped Heliodorus because he tried to take the funds.
“They that were with him took him up, and put him into a litter.”
The high priest “offered a sacrifice for the health of the man”, praying for him so that the king would not think the Jews had done treachery.

Simon, “having been a bewraye of the money, and of his country, slandered Onias.” Out of his hatred he became a betrayer of his own country, willing to destroy his own people to destroy Onias, and made it seem as though Onias “had terrified Heliodorus”. Onias was not on steady ground, but he was a righteous man doing right.

“Jason the brother of Onias laboured underhand to be high priest.” While Onias was going through all that, his own brother, a slimy snake, saw him weakened and moved to take the high priesthood. He couldn’t wait on his ministry.

“For the training up of youth in the fashions of the heathen.” He said, give me the high priesthood and money, and I will turn these people into Greeks and teach them to sin against God: give me a voice and I’ll have you eating brisket at Passover.
Jason sent “Menelaus, the aforesaid Simon’s brother.” You can’t make this up: Simon tried to destroy his nation over Onias, Jason snaked Onias, and now Jason is dealing with Simon’s brother.
Menelaus came “having the fury of a cruel tyrant, and the rage of a savage beast.” He snaked Jason. All of this is envy and jealousy among them.
“Then Jason, who had undermined his own brother, being undermined by another, was compelled to flee.” The treachery is unreal. These are betrayers, and at the end they die.
